testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of tie-down equipment?
questions.explanation: Use the correct number of tie-downs to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer. Examples of tie-down equipment are ropes, straps, and chains.

questions.question: When checking your tires before a trip, you should look at:
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that your tire pressure is not too low or too high.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should use turn signals:

options.text: Only if another vehicle is close by

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal before turning or changing lanes. Do not assume other drivers will move just because you signal.

questions.question: A posted speed limit on a curve:

options.text: Can still cause a vehicle to tip over

questions.correctAnswerText: Can still cause a vehicle to tip over
questions.explanation: A posted speed limit on a curve may be safe for cars but too fast for larger vehicles like trucks. Driving a truck at the posted limit on a curve could cause it to tip over.

questions.question: When starting a truck with a trailer, how do you know if the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working?

options.text: The yellow light on the rear of the trailer stays on
The red light on the trailer flashes three times and then stays on
All rear lights on the trailer flash and then shut off
The blue light near the driver's door lights up

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the rear of the trailer stays on
questions.explanation: Trailers with ABS have a yellow warning light on the left rear. If this light stays on after the engine starts, the ABS is not working.

questions.question: If there is a cargo fire in a box trailer, you should:

options.text: Put a large, heavy blanket over the trailer

questions.explanation: Do not open trailer doors during a cargo fire, especially if the cargo is hazardous. Opening the doors adds oxygen and makes the fire bigger.

questions.question: Move over laws require drivers approaching a stopped emergency vehicle to:

options.text: Move to a lane that is not next to the stopped vehicle
Move to the far side of their lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a lane that is not next to the stopped vehicle
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is stopped on a multilane road, move out of the lane next to it if you can. If you cannot move over safely, slow down and drive with care.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, you should check the hoses for:

options.text: Whether they are connected to the battery
Whether they have the right amount of play

questions.explanation: When inspecting a vehicle with power steering, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels for leaks.

questions.question: On newer vehicles, how do you set the parking brake?

options.text: Move a lever to the right
Push in the yellow diamond-shaped knob
Pull out the yellow diamond-shaped knob
Pull up on the steering column

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull out the yellow diamond-shaped knob
questions.explanation: On newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled by a yellow diamond-shaped knob. Pull it out to set the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: Which of the following is most likely to cause hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is most likely to happen on wet roads when tire pressure is low or tire tread is worn. Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: What do header boards do?

options.text: Protect the driver from cargo that shifts during a crash or sudden stop.
Protect the driver's head when entering the truck cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo that shifts during a crash or sudden stop.
questions.explanation: Header boards (also called headache racks) protect the driver if cargo moves forward during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: The ____ between an air compressor and reservoir tank stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is placed between the air compressor and the main reservoir. It prevents air from leaking out of the system if the compressor fails.

questions.question: What happens with rough acceleration?

options.text: It is normal if the vehicle is warmed up.

questions.explanation: Always accelerate slowly and smoothly. Jerky acceleration can cause mechanical damage to the vehicle.

questions.question: The faster you drive:

options.text: The shorter your stopping distance will be.
The longer your stopping distance will be.
The easier it will be to stop your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer your stopping distance will be.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds require longer distances to stop. Always adjust your braking for your speed.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must be:

options.text: A U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
Able to perform your own background check.

questions.correctAnswerText: A U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
questions.explanation: You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident to get a hazardous materials endorsement. You will lose this endorsement if you give up your U.S. citizenship.

questions.question: When backing up, what is best to do?

options.text: Use only the passenger's side mirror.
Turn toward the passenger's side when possible.

questions.explanation: Back up slowly and check both mirrors. Use a helper to watch your blind spots whenever you can. You and your helper should agree on a stop signal.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, where should the heaviest cargo go?

options.text: On top of the lighter cargo.
At the back of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Keep vehicles balanced and low. Top-heavy vehicles are more likely to roll over. Place heavy cargo under lighter cargo.

questions.question: Which is required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must carry emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, reflective triangles or flares, and at least one working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What does rough acceleration do?

options.text: Is needed to warm up engine parts.
Should be done on slippery surfaces.

questions.explanation: Always accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration causes mechanical damage.

questions.question: Emergency brakes are:

options.text: Only required when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the parking brake.
Put the gearshift in first gear.

questions.explanation: Before checking the engine compartment, use the parking brake and block the wheels. Always check the engine compartment before you get in the cab and start the engine.

questions.question: Before a trip, what should you check about the pedals?

options.text: The gas pedal should be loose.
The pedal surfaces should still have their grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pedal surfaces should still have their grooves.
questions.explanation: Check that nothing is under or around the pedals that could block them. Make sure the pedals work properly. If the pedals have grooves, check that they have not worn smooth.

questions.question: What happens if you stay in neutral too long when shifting gears?

options.text: You may have trouble moving into the next gear.
The vehicle will be hard to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble moving into the next gear.
questions.explanation: If you stay in neutral too long when shifting, it may be hard to put the vehicle into the next gear.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, what should you use mainly to slow down?
questions.explanation: On a steep hill, use the engine to control your speed. Slow down and downshift before you start going down the hill. Using only the brakes can make them too hot and cause them to fail.

questions.question: How should you do pre-trip inspections?

options.text: Do them differently each time to check different items.
Do them the same way each time so you do not forget anything.
Do them once in a while.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do them the same way each time so you do not forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-trip inspection the same way before every trip. This helps you learn all the steps and makes sure you do not skip anything.

questions.question: If you meet an aggressive driver, what should you do?

options.text: Do not respond to their hand gestures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not respond to their hand gestures.
questions.explanation: When you meet an aggressive driver, get out of their way if you can. Do not look at them. Do not respond to any hand gestures they make.

questions.question: How often should you check your cargo during a trip?

options.text: Only at the start of the trip.

questions.explanation: Check your cargo and its straps before you start. After you start, check them within the first 50 miles, then every 3 hours or 150 miles, and after every rest stop.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning usually happen?

options.text: When tires have the right air pressure.
When you drive slower than 15 mph.
Where water pools on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where water pools on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens where water builds up on the road. It can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water. Under-inflated tires or worn tread make it more likely to happen.

questions.question: If you meet an aggressive driver, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you meet an aggressive driver, get away from them. Do not look at them and do not make hand signals. Call the police once you are safe.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check the windshield washer fluid level.

questions.explanation: When checking the engine compartment, check the oil, coolant, and windshield washer fluid. Do not drain or empty the brake fluid.

questions.question: How can you avoid a crash?

options.text: Braking is always the best option.
Swerving may work better than braking.
Drivers should keep 100 yards between their vehicle and the next one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may work better than braking.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest way to avoid a hazard. You can turn to avoid an obstacle faster than you can stop.

questions.question: Looking ahead while driving is:

options.text: Not helpful, since you cannot control things far away.
Good practice to spot hazards early.
Only needed when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Good practice to spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This helps you spot hazards early and have time to respond safely.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly to stay in control. This also gives other drivers time to move if you did not see them. Always use your turn signal.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, the coolant temperature gauge should:

options.text: Slowly rise to normal operating temperature.
Jump quickly to normal operating temperature.
Flash until it reaches normal operating temperature.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly rise to normal operating temperature.
questions.explanation: Watch the gauges after you start the engine. The coolant temperature gauge should rise slowly to the normal operating range.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a sign of when to shift to a higher gear?
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift to a higher gear: engine speed (RPM) and road speed (mph). Check your vehicle's manual for the right RPM range. Watch your speedometer and shift up as needed based on speed.

questions.question: If you stop on the road or shoulder, you must place warning devices within 10 minutes:

options.text: Stand behind your vehicle and wave traffic past.

questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, place emergency warning devices like reflective triangles within 10 minutes of stopping.

questions.question: How do you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times and hold it for five seconds. If it moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down and release. If it does not return to normal, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down and release. If you hear a squeak, there may be a problem.
Remove the rear wheel and listen for noise when the brake pedal is pressed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times and hold it for five seconds. If it moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic brakes by pumping the pedal three times, then pressing it firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or other brake problem.

questions.question: When visibility is poor, like at dawn or dusk, how do you make your vehicle more visible?
questions.explanation: In poor visibility (dawn, dusk, rain, or snow), turn on your low beam headlights to make your vehicle easier to see. Do not use high beams near other vehicles.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:

options.text: The tires need to be replaced.

questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check that the nuts are tight if you see rust.

questions.question: What is a tire load?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
The weight of the tire itself

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum safe weight that a tire can carry at a certain pressure.

questions.question: For a vehicle with air brakes, check the air compressor drive belt before each drive. What condition should the belt be in?
questions.explanation: Check the belt on your air compressor. It should be tight and in good condition.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Creates a loud squeaking noise when being used.
Helps you stay in control while braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you stay in control while braking.
questions.explanation: ABS gives you better control when braking. It does not change how far your vehicle needs to stop.

questions.question: What is true about transporting livestock on a trailer?

options.text: A law enforcement officer must inspect it.
The animals can move and shift, causing unsafe handling.
Only registered farmers can transport it.

questions.correctAnswerText: The animals can move and shift, causing unsafe handling.
questions.explanation: Livestock move and shift their weight during transport. This can make the trailer unsafe to handle.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning signal activates while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop where you are and park
Exit the roadway as soon as safely possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the roadway as soon as safely possible
questions.explanation: When the low pressure warning activates, safely exit the roadway and park. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: A safety belt should:
questions.explanation: Check that your safety belt is secure, adjusts properly, latches firmly, and is not ripped or frayed.

questions.question: When approaching a construction worker near the road, you should:
questions.explanation: Drive carefully through work zones. Slow down when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Is a good way to stay awake on long trips.
Can damage the engine and transmission.
Should be used to prevent rust from forming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can damage the engine and transmission.
questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can damage your vehicle's engine and transmission.

questions.question: Before driving down a hill, you should:
questions.explanation: Switch to a low gear before going downhill. Gravity will speed up your vehicle, so use a low gear to control your speed.

questions.question: Most CDL holders have ____ licenses.
questions.explanation: Most CDL holders drive commercial vehicles across state lines and are non-excepted interstate commerce drivers.

questions.question: An underloaded front axle:

options.text: Is encouraged since front axles are weaker than other axles.
Can cause steering problems and should be avoided.
Improves fuel efficiency and should be done.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause steering problems and should be avoided.
questions.explanation: Do not underload the front axle. It can make steering unsafe. Balance your cargo weight carefully.
